relevance_note: Single-patient first-in-human enzyme replacement report in a man with familial LCAT deficiency: "A 52-year-old male with FLD and ESRD previously described ^16".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; one in-scope person (the single unnamed subject, labelled 'patient' by rule 5). No variants table rows: the paper prints no LCAT variant and never attributes a variant or zygosity to this patient; only reference [16]'s title mentions a 'new loss of function mutation' (homozygous), which is a citation title, not a statement about this patient, so nothing was taken from it. Age '52-year-old' is the age at enrollment, recorded as age at last evaluation (study ran about 8 months after). Lp-X is recorded observed from FPLC/gel statements, but the Discussion says there was no direct measurement of Lp-X (indirect evidence only); noted in severity_or_detail. Baseline TG 147 mg/dL, TC 80 mg/dL, cystatin C and BUN are printed as values without being called abnormal, so no feature rows or checklist status were derived from them. Table 1 (longitudinal renal/hematology values during treatment) was not transcribed beyond the baseline values quoted from the text. Contradiction within the paper (not about phenotype): the Abstract gives optimization doses '0.3, 3.0, and 9.0 mg/kg' while Methods, Results and figure legends give 0.9 mg/kg. Table 1 footnotes are duplicated in the conversion. Full clinical history is said to be in an Online Supplement that is not in the file.
